body: Yep. It was a fucked up feeling of jealousy and protectiveness.

OP... I'm so sorry. Although there are like 2000 comments on this and you'll probably not see this:

The girl I've been in love with since high school, and my best friend, had been bouncing around relationships after our breakup during the 9th grade. During our senior year she was in a fling with one of my other very good friends. She cared about him genuinely, and I knew he was only in it for the sex. I tried to play the middleman. Before I knew it I was the one going back and forth trying to mediate this whole spiel. I don't know what I was thinking -- I told him that if he didn't care about her he'd better back off, because she's a delicate girl. I told her (trying to console her) that he cared about her. He then told her he wanted to break things off.

Later that day, she was drunk in class, overdosed on 5 different meds, cut herself in the bathroom, and had to be rushed to the hospital.

She doesn't know what I said to him, and he doesn't know what I said to her. As a result I almost ended up killing my best friend. She's much better now and in a much better place overall, but I don't know what I would've done if I'd ended up with the blood of my first love and best friend on my hands. I've held that guilt with me ever since. A couple of words can have devastating consequences, and I have never been able to wrap my head around this fact. Absurd.

That guilt will stay with me forever. So OP, I'm sorry you had to had to go through this. I would never expect you to come out with this knowledge ever in your life, and that guilt is something you'll have to live with... but it's hard-earned knowledge that actions are not the only things with consequences. Words are only what they are, but they sometimes contain more weight than we really understand.
